## Purpose and Entry Points
Apache Tomcat is a Java servlet container implementing Jakarta Servlet, Pages/JSP, Expression Language, and WebSocket APIs. Runtime startup is invoked through platform scripts such as `bin/catalina.sh` and `bin/startup.sh`; these bootstrap `org.apache.catalina.startup.Bootstrap` and `Catalina`. The embedded/programmatic entry surface is `java/org/apache/catalina/startup/Tomcat.java`.

## Bootstrap, Configuration, and Lifecycle
`Catalina` loads server configuration, builds the `Server → Service → Engine → Host → Context → Wrapper` container hierarchy, and starts lifecycle-managed components. `conf/server.xml` is the principal server topology/configuration boundary; `conf/catalina.properties` supplies runtime properties. Core concrete container implementations are `java/org/apache/catalina/core/StandardServer.java`, `java/org/apache/catalina/core/StandardService.java`, and `java/org/apache/catalina/core/StandardContext.java`. Deployment and annotation/web-descriptor processing occurs through `java/org/apache/catalina/startup/HostConfig.java` and `java/org/apache/catalina/startup/ContextConfig.java`.

## Network and Protocol Boundary
Socket acceptance, TLS, and NIO buffering live beneath the servlet container in `java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/NioEndpoint.java` and `java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SSLHostConfig.java`. Coyote parses and processes HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and AJP protocol traffic: `java/org/apache/coyote/http11/Http11Processor.java`, `java/org/apache/coyote/http2/Http2Protocol.java`, and `java/org/apache/coyote/ajp/AjpProcessor.java`. Protocol handlers pass normalized request/response objects through the Coyote-to-Catalina adapter, `java/org/apache/catalina/connector/CoyoteAdapter.java`.

## Request Routing and Application Execution
Within Catalina, the connector maps a request to virtual host, web application, and servlet via `java/org/apache/catalina/mapper/Mapper.java`. The container pipeline applies engine/host/context/wrapper valves, then executes the application filter chain and target servlet through `java/org/apache/catalina/core/StandardPipeline.java`, `java/org/apache/catalina/core/ApplicationFilterChain.java`, and `java/org/apache/catalina/core/StandardWrapperValve.java`. Servlet-facing request/response facades isolate application code from internal connector objects in `java/org/apache/catalina/connector/RequestFacade.java` and `java/org/apache/catalina/connector/ResponseFacade.java`.

## Web Application Isolation and State
Each deployed Context owns class loading, resources, naming, sessions, and security configuration. Webapp class-loader isolation is implemented by `java/org/apache/catalina/loader/WebappClassLoaderBase.java`; filesystem/JAR/WAR resources are abstracted by `java/org/apache/catalina/webresources/StandardRoot.java`. Sessions are managed locally through `java/org/apache/catalina/session/StandardManager.java` and `java/org/apache/catalina/session/StandardSession.java`, with file or JDBC persistence options. JNDI resources bridge applications to configured services via `java/org/apache/naming/NamingContext.java` and `java/org/apache/naming/factory/ResourceFactory.java`.

## Security, Dynamic Content, and WebSockets
Authentication and authorization are pipeline concerns: authenticators in `java/org/apache/catalina/authenticator/AuthenticatorBase.java` delegate identity/role lookup to configured realms such as `java/org/apache/catalina/realm/RealmBase.java`. JSP requests reach Jasper’s compiler/runtime, centered on `java/org/apache/jasper/servlet/JspServlet.java` and `java/org/apache/jasper/compiler/Compiler.java`; EL is implemented by `java/org/apache/el/ExpressionFactoryImpl.java`. WebSocket upgrade and server endpoint dispatch are provided by `java/org/apache/tomcat/websocket/server/WsServerContainer.java` and `java/org/apache/tomcat/websocket/server/WsHttpUpgradeHandler.java`.

## Operations, Extensions, and Runtime Dependencies
JMX management is exposed by Catalina MBeans, including `java/org/apache/catalina/mbeans/MBeanFactory.java`; logging uses JULI (`java/org/apache/juli/ClassLoaderLogManager.java`) configured by `conf/logging.properties`. Clustering/session replication uses Catalina HA and Tribes transport, notably `java/org/apache/catalina/ha/tcp/SimpleTcpCluster.java` and `java/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/GroupChannel.java`; cloud membership can integrate with Kubernetes via `java/org/apache/catalina/tribes/membership/cloud/KubernetesMembershipProvider.java`. The primary runtime is a JVM; TLS may use JSSE or optional OpenSSL/native integrations. JDBC databases, LDAP/JNDI, mail, and external load balancers are optional, configuration-driven services rather than mandatory infrastructure.
